answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to post a small time-locked stake before it may transact, then mirror that stake into a reputation ledger where peers record verified work. A new identity starts on a barren island of trust: no history, no credit, so it must complete paid micro-tasks and earn endorsements from established agents before its limit rises. Attackers face an umber cost curve: every fake identity must fund its own stake and grind real work, so a thousand Sybils cost a thousand stakes plus the labor, while honest agents pay once and reuse their reputation.
